name: Acacia
description: Wattles: fast-growing, nitrogen-fixing shrubs and trees with fluffy yellow flowers that are rich in pollen but have no nectar.
care_note: Most wattles live for 10 to 20 years and grow quickly, so they make good nurse plants for slower natives.

name: Agapanthus
description: Clumping plants from southern Africa with round heads of blue or white flowers in summer.

toxic.note: The sap irritates skin and the plant is poisonous if eaten.

care_note: Please cut off the flower heads after flowering, before they set seed. Agapanthus is an environmental weed in parts of Victoria and New South Wales.

name: Allium
description: Onions, garlic, leeks and chives.

toxic.note: Onions, garlic, leeks and chives damage the red blood cells of dogs and cats, raw or cooked.

name: Anigozanthos
description: Kangaroo paws: strappy plants with furry, claw-shaped flowers on tall stems, visited by honeyeaters.
care_note: Cut spent flower stems to the base. Ink disease blackens the leaves in humid weather; please remove affected leaves.

name: Banksia
description: Banksias: Australian shrubs and trees with cylindrical flower spikes that feed honeyeaters, possums and insects.

name: Brassica
description: Cabbages, broccoli, cauliflower, kale and their relatives.
care_note: Cabbage white butterfly caterpillars are the main pest. Fine netting keeps the butterflies off.

name: Callistemon
description: Bottlebrushes. Botanists now place most of them in Melaleuca, but nurseries still sell them as Callistemon.
pruning: Prune just behind the spent flowers to keep plants dense and encourage another flush.

name: Camellia
description: Evergreen shrubs with glossy leaves and large flowers in autumn and winter.
fertiliser_note: Please use an azalea and camellia food, which keeps the soil acidic.

name: Citrus
description: Lemons, limes, oranges, mandarins and their relatives.
fertiliser_note: Please feed with a citrus food in late winter and again in late summer, and water well before and after.

toxic.note: The oils in the leaves and peel can upset cats and dogs.

care_note: Citrus gall wasp, stink bugs and leaf miner are common pests in eastern Australia. The orchard swallowtail butterfly lays its eggs on citrus.

name: Corymbia
description: Bloodwoods and spotted gums, close relatives of the eucalypts.

name: Correa
description: Native fuchsias: small shrubs with bell-shaped flowers through autumn and winter.

name: Cucurbita
description: Pumpkins, squash and zucchini.
care_note: If young fruit shrivels, the flowers were not pollinated. Please brush pollen from a male flower onto the female flowers in the morning.

name: Dianella
description: Flax-lilies: tough strappy plants with small blue or purple flowers and blue berries.

name: Eremophila
description: Emu bushes: dry-country shrubs with tubular flowers that honeyeaters and bees visit.
care_note: Needs very good drainage and struggles in wet, humid summers.

name: Eucalyptus
description: Gum trees, the defining trees of Australian landscapes and the main source of Australian honey.
care_note: Most eucalypts grow into large trees. Please plant them well away from buildings, pipes and paving.

name: Grevillea
description: Grevilleas: Australian shrubs and trees with spidery, nectar-rich flowers that honeyeaters love.
pruning: Tip-prune after each flush of flowers to keep plants dense.

name: Hakea
description: Hakeas: tough Australian shrubs, often prickly, that give small birds safe shelter and nectar.

name: Hibbertia
description: Guinea flowers: Australian shrubs, groundcovers and climbers with bright yellow flowers.

name: Hibiscus
description: Shrubs with large, showy flowers that last a day or two.

name: Hydrangea
description: Deciduous shrubs with large heads of flowers in summer.

toxic.note: The leaves and flower buds contain cyanogenic compounds.

name: Lavandula
description: Lavenders: aromatic shrubs whose flowers draw honey bees and blue-banded bees.
fertiliser_note: Lavender does best in lean soil, which also makes it more fragrant.

toxic.note: Large amounts of the plant or its oil can upset cats and dogs.

name: Leptospermum
description: Tea trees, with small white or pink flowers that feed a wide range of native bees, flies and beetles.

name: Lomandra
description: Mat-rushes: tough tussocks that shelter frogs, lizards and small birds.
pruning: Cut tired clumps back hard, to 10 to 20 cm, every few years.

name: Melaleuca
description: Paperbarks and, since botanists merged the two groups, most bottlebrushes.

name: Mentha
description: Mints.
care_note: Mint spreads quickly by underground runners. Please grow it in a pot.

name: Neoregelia
description: Bromeliads with a cup of water at the centre of each rosette, where frogs often shelter.

name: Ocimum
description: Basils.

name: Pandorea
description: Australian climbers with trumpet-shaped flowers.

name: Rosa
description: Roses. Single-flowered roses give bees pollen; tightly double flowers offer little.
fertiliser_note: Please feed in early spring and again in summer.
pruning: Prune hard in winter, in July or August in most of Australia.
care_note: Black spot and aphids are common. Good air flow around the plant helps.

name: Salvia
description: Salvias (sages): long-flowering shrubs and perennials loved by bees, butterflies and honeyeaters.

name: Solanum
description: A large genus that includes tomatoes, eggplants and potatoes as well as several weeds. Their flowers release pollen when buzzed.

name: Syzygium
description: Lilly pillies: rainforest trees and shrubs with fluffy flowers and colourful fruit that birds eat.
care_note: Lilly pilly psyllids can blister new leaves. Psyllid-resistant varieties are available.

name: Westringia
description: Native rosemaries: tough shrubs with small flowers for much of the year.
pruning: Clip after flowering. Westringias take hard trimming well.

name: Xanthorrhoea
description: Grass trees: very slow-growing plants whose tall flower spikes swarm with insects and birds.
care_note: Grass trees are easily killed by overwatering or disturbance. Please buy only plants tagged as legally salvaged or grown from seed.
